mainTopic: רבי יהודה's reason for lashes in שילוח הקן, how to send the mother bird, and whether a courtyard acquires dovecote eggs for its owner.
overview: The משנה taught that רבי יהודה says one who takes the mother bird with her young gets מלקות and does not send her away. The גמרא first tries to find his reason. Either he gives lashes even for a לאו שניתק לעשה, or he reads 'שַׁלֵּחַ' as a command that applies only from the start. Two proofs are rejected. Then רבינא brings a ברייתא about leftover meat of the קרבן פסח, and it shows that רבי יהודה gives no lashes for a fixable לאו. So his reason must be that 'שלח' applies from the start. Next the גמרא teaches how far and how to send the bird, and tells stories about רב יהודה, who punished a man for clipping a bird's wings, and about רבא and the תימה bird. A ברייתא rules that dovecote pigeons require sending but are protected by a rabbinic ban on robbery, and the גמרא works out when a courtyard acquires eggs for its owner. The amud ends with a story of שמואל telling רב יהודה to bang on a dovecote. The גמרא begins asking why, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The earlier ברייתא is unreliable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the previous proof. That ברייתא was not taught in the schools of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא, so its wording may be corrupted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any ברייתא that was not taught in the study hall of רבי חייא or the study hall of רבי אושעיא is corrupted, and you may not raise objections from it in the בית מדרש. Perhaps the real wording was 'is NOT included among those who get forty lashes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof it just brought. It says the ברייתא used for that proof is not trustworthy, because it did not come from the careful schools of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא seemed to quote רבי יהודה as saying a לאו שניתק לעשה does carry מלקות. The גמרא says the text may be garbled, and perhaps it really said 'אינה בכלל', that there are no lashes. So this source cannot tell us רבי יהודה's reason; steps 5-6 settle it.

keyTerms.meaning: Corrupted, garbled (a text that was not passed down accurately)
Raise an objection (to challenge someone using a source)
The study hall
The Torah punishment of forty lashes (in practice thirty-nine)
Perhaps, maybe (often used to open a rejection)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי יהודה's opinion is wrong. It is only saying that this particular ברייתא can't be trusted to tell us what he said.

phrases.english: (of the study hall of) Rabbi Ḥiyya and the study hall of Rabbi Oshaya
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started just before: 'Any ברייתא that was not taught in the study hall of...'

phrases.english: is corrupted
and you may not raise objections from it in the study hall
perhaps 'is not included among'
those liable to forty lashes was what was taught

steps.triggerLanguage: מְשַׁבַּשְׁתָּא הִיא, וְלָא תּוֹתְבוּ מִינַּהּ בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought just before this section by questioning whether the ברייתא it relied on is reliable.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole proof by undermining the reliability of its source text.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא did not come from the schools of רבי חייא and רבי אושעיא, so its wording may be corrupted. It may really have said 'אינה בכלל מלקות'.

steps.title: A reliable ברייתא about שכחה and פאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from רבי אושעיא and רבי חייא. In it, רבי יהודה says that one who goes back for a forgotten sheaf, or harvests the corner of his field, gets מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבי אושעיא and רבי חייא taught: 'Do not go back' (for a forgotten sheaf), and he went back; 'Do not finish off' (the corner of the field), and he finished it off. Such people are included among those who get forty lashes. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a new source that does come from the reliable schools. It sets up a proof about רבי יהודה's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שכחה and פאה each have a לאו, and they also have a positive מצוה to leave the produce for the poor. That makes them look like classic cases of לאו שניתק לעשה. Since רבי יהודה gives lashes here, this ברייתא may show his general approach.

keyTerms.meaning: A forgotten sheaf, which must be left for the poor
The corner of the field, which must be left for the poor
'Do not go back' (the לאו of שכחה)
'Do not finish off' (the לאו of פאה)
They are included in (the punishment)

phrases.english: Come and hear
that which Rabbi Oshaya and Rabbi Ḥiyya taught
'You shall not return,' and he returned
'You shall not wholly reap,' and he wholly reaped
they are included among those liable to forty lashes
this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the unreliable ברייתא, the גמרא brings one that comes from the trusted schools.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's reason in the מִשְׁנָה is that he holds לאו שניתק לעשה לוקין עליו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי אושעיא and רבי חייא: according to רבי יהודה, one who violates the לאו of שכחה or פאה gets מלקות.

steps.title: The proof: רבי יהודה gives lashes for a לאו שניתק לעשה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws its conclusion from the ברייתא. רבי יהודה must hold that one gets lashes for a לאו שניתק לעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the reason of רבי יהודה is that he holds one gets lashes for a לאו that is fixed by a positive מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the ברייתא seems to prove about רבי יהודה's reason in the מִשְׁנָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שכחה and פאה come with the עשה of 'לעני ולגר תעזב אתם', so they are a לאו שניתק לעשה. If רבי יהודה still gives מלקות there, the same logic would explain his ruling about the mother bird. That would answer the open question.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (introduces a conclusion drawn from a source)
His reason
A prohibition that can be 'fixed' by doing a positive מצוה afterward
One gets lashes for it

phrases.english: Conclude from it that the reason of Rabbi Yehuda
is because he holds
that a prohibition that is fixed by a positive מצוה
one is flogged for it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the intended conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה holds לאו שניתק לעשה לוקין עליו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His ruling of lashes for שכחה and פאה, which have both a לאו and an עשה.

steps.title: Maybe 'תעזוב' means from the outset
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יהודה may hold that 'תעזוב' (leave them) applies only from the start, so שכחה and פאה are not really cases of a fixable לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps there (by שכחה and פאה) this is the reason: he holds that 'you shall leave' implies from the very start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It offers a different reason why רבי יהודה gives lashes for שכחה and פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'תעזוב' means you must leave the produce from the start, then once a person takes it, the עשה can no longer be fulfilled. In that case the לאו was never really fixable. So the ברייתא does not prove that רבי יהודה gives lashes for a true לאו שניתק לעשה, and his ruling about the mother bird could rest on the same idea: that 'שַׁלֵּחַ' applies from the outset.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in that other case)
'You shall leave' (the עשה of leaving produce for the poor)
From the start, from the outset
Implies, means

steps.whatToRemember: Neither proof works. The first ברייתא may be corrupted, and the second can be explained by reading 'תעזוב' as 'from the outset'. So these sources cannot prove רבי יהודה's reason in the מִשְׁנָה. רבינא's ברייתא in steps 5-6 settles it.

phrases.english: Perhaps there, this is the reason
that he holds that 'you shall leave'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:10, 'לעני ולגר תעזב אתם', the positive מצוה of שכחה and פאה.

phrases.english: implies from the outset

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 3 by giving another explanation for רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference about רבי יהודה's general principle. It does not reject the ברייתא itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling of lashes for שכחה and פאה could come from reading 'תעזוב' as 'from the outset', and not from a general rule that one gets lashes for a לאו שניתק לעשה.

steps.title: רבינא brings a ברייתא about leftover meat of the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says that a positive command placed after a prohibition means there are no lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear: 'You shall leave none of it until morning... you shall burn it in fire.' The verse places a positive command after a prohibition to teach you that there are no lashes for it. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a new source to show what רבי יהודה really holds about a לאו that can be fixed by a positive command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: About leftover meat of the קרבן פסח, the תורה first forbids leaving it over, and then commands to burn what is left. רבי יהודה says the תורה put the burning command there to tell us there are no lashes. So רבי יהודה does NOT give lashes for a לאו that has a fixing עשה after it.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not leave any over (the prohibition on leftover meat of the פסח)
The verse comes to teach
A positive command placed after a prohibition
They give lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear:
"You shall not leave any of it until morning
etc.… you shall burn in fire"
phrases.notes: שמות 12:10. This is about the meat of the קרבן פסח.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא הַכָּתוּב לִיתֵּן עֲשֵׂה אַחַר לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: The verse comes to place a positive command after a prohibition,
to tell you that one does not get lashes for it,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 4 suggested that רבי יהודה reads the command as applying only from the start, רבינא brings a source that forces this reading.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה does not give lashes for a לאו שניתק לעשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on נותר of the קרבן פסח (שמות 12:10)

steps.title: So רבי יהודה reads 'send away' as applying from the start
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי יהודה gives no lashes for a fixable לאו, his reason in our משנה must be that 'שלח' applies only from the start. The גמרא agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: the reason of רבי יהודה is that he holds 'send away' means from the very start. Indeed, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא, and the גמרא agrees with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה never gives lashes for a fixable לאו, yet he gives lashes for taking the mother bird, then for him this לאו must not be fixable. That works only if 'שלח' is a command for the start, before taking, and not a way to fix the sin afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: Send away (the mother bird)
It means from the very start
The reason
Learn from this / it is proven

steps.confusionAlert: 'שמע מינה' appears twice. The first one is רבינא drawing his conclusion. The second one is the גמרא agreeing: 'Yes, that's proven.'
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, there are no lashes for a לאו שניתק לעשה. He gives lashes in אם על הבנים only because he reads 'שלח' as applying from the start.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
the reason of Rabbi Yehuda
is because he holds
that "send away" means from the very start.
Indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא in step 5 and confirms the suggestion of step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה's reason for lashes in אם על הבנים is that 'שלח' applies only from the start, not that he gives lashes for a לאו שניתק לעשה.

steps.title: רב אידי supports this from the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי says the משנה's wording 'he gets lashes and does not send away' fits this reading. If the לאו were fixable, it should say 'he gets lashes and sends away.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי said to רב אשי: Our משנה is also precise this way. It teaches: one who takes the mother with the young, רבי יהודה says, he gets lashes and does not send away. If you thought רבי יהודה's reason is that one gets lashes for a לאו שניתק לעשה, it should have said 'he gets lashes and sends away'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי brings extra support for the same conclusion, this time from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sending away were a way to fix the לאו, the מצוה of sending would still apply, and the משנה would say 'he sends away.' Since it says 'he does not send away,' the sending must have been only a command for the start, which is now too late.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise, supports this reading from its wording
The mother bird together with her young
A prohibition that can be fixed by a positive command
If it would enter your mind
It should have said

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אִידִי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Idi said to Rav Ashi:
Our Mishnah is also precise this way,
as it teaches: one who takes the mother with the young —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לוֹקֶה וְאֵין מְשַׁלֵּחַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: he gets lashes and does not send away.
And if it would enter your mind
that Rabbi Yehuda's reason is
that one gets lashes for a prohibition fixable by a positive command,
he should have said "he gets lashes and sends away"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second support for the conclusion of step 6, this time from the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: For רבי יהודה, אם על הבנים is not a לאו שניתק לעשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of our משנה: 'לוקה ואין משלח'

steps.title: The משנה's wording can be read differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אידי's proof. 'אין משלח' could mean that sending away alone does not clear him; he is not cleared until he gets lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps this is what it means in the משנה: he is not cleared until they give him lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אידי and shows that the wording of the משנה does not prove his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אידי read 'אין משלח' as 'there is no more מצוה to send.' The גמרא suggests it may mean 'sending does not free him.' He may still send the bird, but he stays guilty until he gets lashes. So the משנה's wording is no proof. The conclusion of step 6 still stands, because it rests on the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
Cleared / free of guilt
They give lashes

phrases.english: But perhaps this is what it is saying in the Mishnah:
he is not cleared until they give him lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אידי's wording-based proof from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב אידי's proof from the משנה's wording. The ברייתא-based conclusion of step 6 is untouched.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'אין משלח' can mean 'sending does not clear him without lashes,' and not 'there is no מצוה to send.'

steps.title: How far must he send the mother bird?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how far away the mother bird must be sent.
steps.simpleTranslation: How far must he send her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question: when someone sends away the mother bird, how far must she go? This sets up רב יהודה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן in the משנה said that even after taking the mother he must send her away. Now the גמרא wants to know what counts as properly sending her.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of sending away the mother bird from the nest
He sends her away

phrases.english: How far must he send her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יהודה and רבנן debate and opens a practical question about how sending works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum distance the mother bird must be sent.

steps.title: Far enough that she leaves his grasp
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says she must be sent far enough that she is out of his hand's reach.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Far enough that she goes out from under his hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers: she only needs to get far enough that he can no longer simply grab her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no fixed distance. The rule is that she must be truly free, out of his control, so he cannot just catch her right away.

keyTerms.meaning: From under his hand, out of his control or reach

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Enough that she goes out from under his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּצֵא מִתַּחַת יָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She must be sent out of his grasp, so he can no longer catch her right away.

steps.title: In what way does he send her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how he holds the bird when sending her away.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does he send her?
steps.whatsHappening: A second practical question: by which part of her body does he hold her when he lets her go? This sets up a debate between רב הונא and רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first question was about distance; this one is about the method of sending.

keyTerms.meaning: With what, in what way

phrases.english: With what does he send her?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second practical question following the distance question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The method of sending, meaning which body part he holds.

steps.title: Feet or wings
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says he sends her by her feet; רב יהודה says by her wings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: by her feet. רב יהודה said: by her wings.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree. רב הונא says hold her by the feet, and רב יהודה says hold her by the wings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree she must be sent. They only disagree about the proper way to hold her while letting her go.

keyTerms.meaning: By her feet
By her wings

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: By her feet,
Rav Yehuda said: By her wings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: בְּרַגְלֶיהָ, רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: בַּאֲגַפֶּיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two answers to the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: by the feet. רב יהודה: by the wings.

steps.title: The reasons for feet and for wings
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a פסוק linking sending to feet; רב יהודה says a bird's wings are her feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said by her feet, as it is written: 'That send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey.' רב יהודה said by her wings, because they are her feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains each opinion. רב הונא brings a פסוק that connects 'sending' with feet, and רב יהודה answers that for a bird, the wings do the job of feet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא learns from the word 'משלחי' next to 'רגל' that sending goes with the feet. רב יהודה agrees that sending goes with what moves the creature, but a bird moves with her wings, so for her the wings count as feet.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who send forth the foot, from the פסוק in ישעיה
Her wings

phrases.english: Rav Huna said by her feet,
as it is written: 'That send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey.'
Rav Yehuda said by her wings,
because her wings are her 'feet.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons behind the two opinions in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's view that sending is by the feet, and רב יהודה's view that it is by the wings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיה 32:20, 'משלחי רגל השור והחמור', plus the logic that a bird's wings serve as her feet.

steps.title: The man who clipped the bird's wings
steps.stepSummary: A man clipped a mother bird's wings, sent her, and caught her again. רב יהודה gave him lashes and told him to let the wings grow and send her properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man clipped her wings, sent her away, and afterward caught her. רב יהודה gave him lashes. He said to him: Go let her wings grow and send her away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. A man tried a trick: he clipped the bird's wings so she could not fly, 'sent' her, and then easily caught her. רב יהודה punished him with lashes and ordered him to send her properly once her wings grow back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sending a bird that cannot fly is not real sending, because she never truly leaves his control, as step 10 required. So רב יהודה demands a real sending, and also gives lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: He cut, clipped
He gave him lashes
Her wings

phrases.english: A certain man who clipped her wings,
and sent her away, and afterward caught her.
Rav Yehuda gave him lashes.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זִיל רַבִּי לַהּ גַּדְפַיהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Go, let her wings grow,
and send her away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real-life case connected to the rules of how to send her away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה gave both lashes and an order to send the bird away properly.

steps.title: Whose opinion did רב יהודה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: giving lashes and requiring sending fits neither רבי יהודה nor the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? If like רבי יהודה, he gets lashes and does not send. If like the רבנן, he sends and does not get lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's ruling. In the משנה, רבי יהודה says lashes without sending, and the רבנן say sending without lashes, so how could רב יהודה require both?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side of the משנה's dispute asks for lashes and sending together. רב יהודה's ruling seems to mix the two opinions, which neither one allows.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom, whose opinion does this follow
He receives lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two names. רב יהודה, the אמורא who gave the lashes, is a different person from רבי יהודה, the תנא of the משנה.

phrases.english: According to whom?

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה – לוֹקֶה וְאֵין מְשַׁלֵּחַ,
phrases.english: If like Rabbi Yehuda, he gets lashes and does not send away;
if like the Rabbis, he sends away and does not get lashes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in the story of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling of lashes together with sending.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's two opinions each give only one result (lashes or sending), never both.

steps.title: Like the רבנן, and the lashes were rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה followed the רבנן; the lashes were מכת מרדות, a rabbinic punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really he follows the רבנן, and the lashes were מכת מרדות, from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: רב יהודה followed the רבנן, who require sending. The lashes were not Torah lashes but a rabbinic punishment for the man's bad behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Torah lashes and sending do not go together according to the רבנן. But חכמים may give their own lashes, מכת מרדות, to someone who acts defiantly, as this man did with his trick.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping the first option)
Lashes for rebelliousness, a rabbinic punishment
By rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: The sending follows the רבנן's Torah law; the lashes were only a rabbinic מכת מרדות for the man's trickery.

phrases.english: Really, it follows the Rabbis,
and the lashes were rabbinic lashes for rebelliousness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the lashes as a different kind of punishment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lashes seemed to be Torah lashes, which would clash with requiring sending.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sending follows the רבנן, and the lashes were rabbinic מכת מרדות.

steps.title: A man asks רבא about the תימה
steps.stepSummary: A man asks רבא what the law is for the bird called תימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבא and said to him: What about a תימה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. A man asks רבא whether the מצוה of sending applies to a certain bird called תימה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question seems to be whether this kind of bird is included in the מצוה at all. רבא's reaction comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of a kind of kosher bird
What is the law?

phrases.english: A certain man who came before Rava,
said to him: What is the law of a teima?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story, unconnected to the wing-clipping case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תימה bird is included in the מצוה of sending.

steps.title: Every kosher bird must be sent
steps.stepSummary: רבא is surprised: doesn't this man know that any kosher bird must be sent?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Doesn't this man know that a kosher bird must be sent away?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is surprised by the question. The תימה is a kosher bird, and every kosher bird is included in the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's surprise shows the basic rule: the מצוה applies to every kosher bird. So the man's doubt must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: A kosher bird

phrases.english: He said: Does this man not know
that for a kosher bird one is obligated to send it away?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא יָדַע הַאי גַּבְרָא דְּעוֹף טָהוֹר חַיָּיב לְשַׁלּוֹחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's first reaction to the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every kosher bird, including the תימה, is included in the מצוה.

steps.title: Maybe the question is about a single egg
steps.stepSummary: רבא guesses that the man's real doubt is about a nest with only one egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Perhaps it is a single egg that is lying there?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to figure out what is really bothering the man. Maybe the תימה's nest had only one egg, and he wondered if that counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'אפרוחים או ביצים' in the plural, so someone might think one egg is not enough. רבא is clarifying the true question.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg
That is lying there

phrases.english: He said to him: Perhaps a single egg
is what is lying there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא looks for the man's real doubt after step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the man's doubt is about a nest with just one egg.

steps.title: The משנה already says one egg obligates sending
steps.stepSummary: The man says yes; רבא answers that a משנה rules even one chick or one egg requires sending.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Yes. רבא said: What is your question? It is a משנה: Even if there is only one chick or one egg, he must send the mother away.
steps.whatsHappening: The man confirms his doubt is about one egg. רבא tells him the answer is already in the משנה: even one chick or one egg obligates sending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural in the פסוק does not mean at least two. The משנה clearly rules that a single egg or chick is enough, so the man had no reason to doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A chick, a baby bird
What is your question? (meaning the answer is obvious)

steps.whatToRemember: Every kosher bird is included in the מצוה, and even a single egg or chick obligates sending away the mother.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording, where the man answers 'yes.'

phrases.english: He said to him: What is your question?
It is our Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא אֶפְרוֹחַ אֶחָד אוֹ בֵיצָה אַחַת –
phrases.english: If there is only one chick or one egg there,
he is obligated to send away the mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין הִיא: אֵין שָׁם אֶלָּא אֶפְרוֹחַ אֶחָד אוֹ בֵיצָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the doubt identified in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה rules that even one chick or one egg obligates sending away the mother.

steps.title: The man sends the bird away and רבא catches it
steps.stepSummary: The man follows רבא's ruling and sends away the mother bird. רבא then surrounds her with nets and catches her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent it away, and רבא surrounded it with nets and caught it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from the last steps finishes. The man does the מצוה and sends the mother away, and then רבא catches her for himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the mother has been sent away, the מצוה is done, so catching her afterward is allowed. This ending sets up the גמרא's next question about how it looked.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent it away (the mother bird)
Nets or traps for catching birds
Caught it

phrases.english: He sent it away,
phrases.notes: "He" is the man who asked רבא about the תימה bird in the last steps.

phrases.english: and רבא surrounded it with nets
and caught it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁלְחַהּ, וְאַהְדַּר לַהּ רָבָא פְּרִסְתָּקֵי וְתַפְסַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story after רבא ruled that even one egg requires sending.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the mother is sent away, רבא was allowed to catch her.

steps.title: Shouldn't רבא worry about looking suspicious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether people might suspect רבא of ruling that the bird must be sent away just so he could catch it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But shouldn't he be concerned about suspicion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a concern about how רבא's action looked. People might think he gave his ruling for his own gain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What רבא did was allowed. The problem is only how it looked: a judge should not appear to profit from his own ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him be concerned
Suspicion, how things look to others

phrases.english: But shouldn't he be concerned about suspicion?
phrases.notes: The worry is that people will think רבא made the man send the bird away just so he could grab it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way רבא behaved in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא catching the bird right after ruling it must be sent away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Catching it right away makes it look as if he ruled for his own benefit.

steps.title: He caught it in an unusual way
steps.stepSummary: רבא caught the bird in an unusual manner, so it did not look connected to his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: In an unusual manner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא caught the bird in a roundabout way, so nobody would link the catch to his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the catch was not done in the normal, direct way, it did not look like he planned it. So there was no reason for suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally "with the back of the hand"; in an unusual, indirect way

phrases.english: In an unusual manner.
phrases.notes: Literally "as if with the back of the hand," meaning not done in the normal way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the concern about suspicion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies how the act was done
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא openly caught the bird, which would look suspicious.
steps.terutzMaskana: He caught it in an unusual manner, so it did not look suspicious.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's story ends cleanly: the man sent the mother away, and רבא caught her in an unusual way so there was no suspicion.

steps.title: Pigeons of a dovecote or attic need sending, but taking them is rabbinic robbery
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that pigeons nesting in a dovecote or attic require שילוח הקן. Taking them is still forbidden as גזל because of דרכי שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Pigeons of a dovecote and pigeons of an attic are obligated in sending away the mother. And taking them is forbidden as robbery because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about pigeons that nest on a person's property. They need שילוח, and taking them is forbidden as robbery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying they need שילוח means the Torah treats these birds as not truly owned by anyone. The robbery ban is only a rabbinic rule, made to keep peace between people.

keyTerms.meaning: Pigeons living in a dovecote (pigeon house)
Pigeons nesting in an attic
Sending away the mother bird (שילוח הקן)
Robbery
Because of the ways of peace; a rabbinic rule to prevent fighting

steps.confusionAlert: The ban on taking the pigeons does not mean they belong to the owner by Torah law. It is only a rabbinic rule for peace, which is why the מצוה of sending still applies.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Pigeons of a dovecote and pigeons of an attic –
are obligated in sending away the mother,
and they are forbidden because of robbery
because of the ways of peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹנֵי שׁוֹבָךְ וְיוֹנֵי עֲלִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story of רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dovecote and attic pigeons require שילוח; taking them is rabbinic גזל because of דרכי שלום.

steps.title: Doesn't a person's courtyard acquire the eggs for him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא using רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא's rule that a courtyard acquires items for its owner even without his knowledge. Then the eggs belong to him, and the פסוק excludes birds that are already his.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the rule of רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא is true, that a person's courtyard acquires for him even without his knowledge, then apply here "if it happens upon you," which excludes something already ready for you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא. If a person's property automatically acquires things for him, the eggs in his dovecote are already his, so the מצוה should not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "כי יקרא" means the מצוה only applies to a nest you happen to find, not one already ready and owned. רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא's rule would make the dovecote eggs owned, which clashes with the ברייתא's ruling that they need שילוח.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's courtyard acquires things for him
Without his knowledge
"If it happens" (a nest you come across by chance)
This excludes something already ready and available to you

phrases.english: But if this is true

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: which Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina said,
a person's courtyard acquires for him
even without his knowledge,
apply here "if it happens" –
which excludes what is readily available!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִיתָא לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's ruling that dovecote pigeons need שילוח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that dovecote and attic pigeons are obligated in שילוח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the courtyard acquires the eggs automatically, they are owned and ready, and the פסוק "כי יקרא" excludes such a nest.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the מצוה of שילוח הקן depends on the nest not already belonging to you.

steps.title: The obligation starts before the courtyard acquires the egg
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the obligation of שילוח begins when most of the egg comes out. The courtyard only acquires it once it falls in, so the ברייתא is talking about that earlier moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: With an egg, once most of it comes out, one is obligated in sending away the mother. But the owner does not acquire it until it falls into his courtyard. And when the ברייתא teaches that they are obligated in sending, it means before it falls into his courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה resolves the challenge by pointing to a short window of time. The מצוה applies when most of the egg has come out, before it lands and becomes the owner's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different moments: the obligation starts when most of the egg has come out, and ownership only starts when it falls into the courtyard. In between, the egg is not yet owned, so it is not "ready" for him and the מצוה applies. So both the ברייתא and רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא's rule can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: The coming out of most of it (the egg)
He does not acquire it
Until it falls into his courtyard
Before

steps.whatToRemember: The obligation of שילוח starts when most of the egg comes out, but the owner's courtyard only acquires it when it falls in. The ברייתא is talking about that in-between moment.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
phrases.notes: Some versions say רב, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is רבה.

phrases.english: An egg – with the coming out of most of it
that is when one becomes obligated in sending,
but he does not acquire it
until it falls into his courtyard,
and when it teaches "they are obligated in sending" –
it means before it falls into his courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: בֵּיצָה עִם יְצִיאַת רוּבָּהּ הוּא דְּאִחַיַּיב בְּשִׁלּוּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a specific time window
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The eggs are owned by the courtyard owner from the start, so שילוח should not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means the moment after most of the egg has come out but before it falls into the courtyard, when it is not yet owned.

steps.title: Why would it be robbery if the egg isn't his yet?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא means the egg is only partly out, it is still part of the mother's body and the owner has not acquired it. So why does the ברייתא forbid taking it, even as robbery only for the sake of peace?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why are they forbidden because of robbery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's answer from step 26. If the egg has not fully come out and fallen into the courtyard, it is still part of the mother's body. Why should there be even a rabbinic ban, for the sake of peace, on taking it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the ברייתא means the moment when most of the egg is out but it hasn't landed in the courtyard. At that moment the courtyard has not acquired anything, and the egg is still part of the mother's body (Rashi). The ברייתא's ban is only rabbinic, for the sake of peace, so the question is why even that ban should apply to an egg that is not yet a separate egg.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
Why?
They are forbidden
Robbery; taking what belongs to someone else

phrases.english: If so,
why are they forbidden because of robbery?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַמַּאי אֲסוּרוֹת מִשּׁוּם גָּזֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 26 using the robbery clause of the ברייתא in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the ברייתא means the moment before the egg fully comes out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An egg still part of the mother's body is not yet a separate thing, so why should even the rabbinic peace-based ban on taking it apply?

steps.title: The robbery rule is about the mother bird
steps.stepSummary: The ban on robbery in the ברייתא is about the mother bird, not the eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It refers to their mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the robbery part of the ברייתא is talking about the mother bird, not the eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eggs are not yet the owner's, so taking them is not robbery. The ברייתא's ban on robbery is about the mother bird that lives in his dovecote.

keyTerms.meaning: On their mother; the ruling is about the mother bird
Mother bird

phrases.english: On their mother.
phrases.notes: He means the robbery rule in the ברייתא is about the mother bird, not the eggs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the ruling onto a different subject: the mother, not the eggs
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The robbery ban was about the eggs, which aren't owned yet
steps.terutzMaskana: The robbery ban is about the mother bird

steps.title: Or: the owner already has his mind on the egg
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the ruling really is about the egg. Once most of it is out, the owner has his mind set on it, so the חכמים called taking it robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: really it is about the egg. Once most of an egg has come out, the owner has his mind set on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to step 27. The robbery ban really is about the egg, because the owner already counts on getting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legally the courtyard has not acquired the egg yet. But once most of it is out, the owner expects it and thinks of it as his. So the חכמים made taking it a form of robbery.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; brings a second answer
Really; actually (keeping the first understanding)
The majority; most of it
His mind is on it; he counts on getting it

phrases.english: Or if you want, say:
really, it is about the egg,
and an egg, once most of it has come out,
his mind is on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 27, in place of step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic robbery based on what the owner expects
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the owner's mind is on the egg, the חכמים treated taking it as robbery

steps.title: With רב's rule, even an egg in the courtyard isn't acquired
steps.stepSummary: רב said you may not acquire eggs while the mother is sitting on them. So the courtyard can't acquire them either, even after they fall in, and שילוח still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that רב יהודה said in the name of רב that it is forbidden to acquire eggs while the mother sits on them, because the פסוק says 'send the mother' and only then 'take the young,' you can even say the ברייתא means eggs that already fell into his courtyard. Wherever he himself can acquire, his courtyard acquires for him. Wherever he can't, his courtyard can't either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the challenge of step 25. Using רב's rule, it says the ברייתא can even mean eggs that already fell into the courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 the problem was that the courtyard acquires the eggs, so the bird would already be his and exempt from שילוח. רב teaches that a person may not acquire eggs while the mother sits on them. A courtyard only acquires what its owner could acquire himself, so it does not acquire these eggs, and the מצוה still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: To acquire; to take ownership
Sitting (resting) on the eggs
And only afterward
His courtyard (his property)
Is able to acquire

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general rule: a person's property can only acquire for him what he could legally acquire himself.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And now that רב יהודה said in the name of רב:
It is forbidden to acquire eggs
that the mother is sitting on,
as it says: "Send away the mother"
and only then "the young you may take for yourself."
you can even say
even though it fell into his courtyard,
wherever he himself can acquire,
his courtyard also acquires,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאִיהוּ לָא מָצֵי זָכֵי
phrases.english: and wherever he himself cannot acquire,
his courtyard also does not acquire for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the challenge of step 25 and offers a different answer than רבה's in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits when a courtyard can acquire, using רב's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the eggs fall into the courtyard, the owner has them and שילוח no longer applies
steps.terutzMaskana: The courtyard can't acquire eggs the owner himself can't acquire, so שילוח still applies even after they fall in
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to acquire eggs while the mother sits on them, and a courtyard acquires only what its owner could acquire

steps.title: Then why is it only a rabbinic robbery?
steps.stepSummary: If the courtyard can't acquire until the mother is sent, then taking the eggs is either full Torah robbery or a failure to do שילוח. Either way it is a Torah matter, so why does the ברייתא call it only דרכי שלום?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why are they forbidden only because of the ways of peace? If he sent the mother away, it is full robbery. If he didn't send her away, he must send her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer from step 30. Taking the eggs seems to break a Torah law either way, not just a rabbinic one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the mother is sent away, the owner can acquire, so his courtyard acquires the eggs at once. Taking them then is real Torah robbery. If she wasn't sent away, the taker himself breaks the מצוה of שילוח. Either way, the ברייתא's light reason of דרכי שלום doesn't fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The ways of peace; a rabbinic rule made to prevent fights
Full, real robbery (from the Torah)
He is required to send her away

phrases.english: If so,
why are they forbidden only because of the ways of peace?
If he sent her away,
it is full robbery,
if he did not send her away,
he needs to send her away!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַמַּאי אֲסוּרוֹת מִפְּנֵי דַּרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 30 that the ברייתא means eggs already in the courtyard
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either case breaks a Torah law (robbery or שילוח), so a merely rabbinic reason like דרכי שלום makes no sense

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a minor
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about a קטן who took the eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is about a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a child who took the eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן is not obligated in the מצוה of שילוח הקן. Since the mother was never sent away, the courtyard never acquired the eggs, so no Torah robbery happened either. Only a rabbinic issue is left.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor; a child not yet obligated in מצוות

phrases.english: With a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about an adult, who breaks a Torah law either way
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a קטן, so only a rabbinic robbery is involved

steps.title: Is a child bound by rabbinic rules?
steps.stepSummary: A minor is not obligated in rabbinic rules either, so how can the ברייתא forbid him because of דרכי שלום?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a minor subject to the ways of peace?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 32. A child isn't obligated in rabbinic rules either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the case to a קטן removed the Torah problem. But a child isn't bound by rabbinic laws either, so the ruling of דרכי שלום doesn't seem to apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Subject to; someone to whom a rule applies

phrases.english: Is a minor subject to the ways of peace?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 32
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about a קטן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A minor is not obligated even in rabbinic rules, so דרכי שלום can't bind him

steps.title: The child's father must return the eggs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means the father of the קטן must return the eggs to the owner, because of דרכי שלום.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: the father of the minor must return it to him, because of the ways of peace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא's ruling is aimed at the child's father, who must give the eggs back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The child himself isn't obligated in anything. But his father is an adult, and the חכמים require him to return the eggs to the dovecote owner to keep peace between people.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; explains a statement
His father
To return

steps.whatToRemember: With רב's rule, eggs under a sitting mother aren't acquired even by the owner's courtyard. The ברייתא's rabbinic robbery case is about a קטן who took them, and his father must return them because of דרכי שלום.

phrases.english: This is what it means:

phrases.english: the father of the minor must return it to him,
phrases.notes: "To him" means to the owner of the dovecote or attic.

phrases.english: because of the ways of peace.

steps.terutzMaskana: The father is required to return the eggs because of דרכי שלום

steps.title: שמואל tells רב יהודה to bang on the nest
steps.stepSummary: לוי בר סימון transferred his dovecote's young birds to רב יהודה. שמואל told רב יהודה to bang on the nest so the birds would rise up and he would acquire them.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי בר סימון gave רב יהודה ownership of the 'produce' of his dovecote. רב יהודה came to שמואל, who told him: Go bang on the nest, so the birds rise up, and acquire them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about acquiring birds from a dovecote. שמואל gives רב יהודה a practical instruction: bang on the nest so the birds lift up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'produce' of a dovecote means the young birds and eggs it produces. שמואל's advice is surprising, because it is not obvious why banging on the nest is needed. That question is exactly what the גמרא will ask next.

keyTerms.meaning: Transferred ownership (gave someone acquisition rights)
The 'produce' of his dovecote, meaning the young birds and eggs
Bang (knock) on the nest
So that they will rise up (be lifted)

phrases.english: Levi bar Simon transferred ownership
of the produce of his dovecote to Rav Yehuda.
phrases.notes: 'Produce' here means the young birds and eggs the dovecote produces, not fruit.

phrases.english: He came before Shmuel.
He said to him: Go, bang on the nest,
so that they rise up, and you will acquire them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵוִי בַּר סִימוֹן אַקְנִי פֵּירוֹת שׁוֹבָכוֹ לְרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא about eggs falling into a courtyard to a new story about acquiring birds from a dovecote.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל instructed רב יהודה to bang on the nest so the birds would rise up and he would acquire them.

steps.title: What was the banging for? Not for buying, since a cloth would work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל told him to bang on the nest. If it was only to finalize the purchase, they could have used a קנין סודר instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose? If it was to acquire the birds, let Levi transfer them to him with a cloth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what שמואל's instruction was for, and knocks out the first possible reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One possibility is that the banging was a way to finalize the purchase. But a simple קנין סודר (acquiring through a cloth) would make the deal binding, so there is no need to bang on the nest. That means the banging must serve some other purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose?
In order to acquire
Acquiring by handing over a cloth, a standard way to make a deal binding

phrases.english: For what purpose?
If it was to acquire,
let him transfer them to him with a cloth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of שמואל's instruction in step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What was the purpose of banging on the nest?
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the banging was meant to finalize the acquisition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קנין סודר would finalize the acquisition easily, so banging on the nest would be pointless for that goal.

steps.title: Second possibility: was it for יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a second possibility: maybe the banging was about getting the birds ready for use on יום טוב. The rest of this thought continues next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was for יום טוב...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It offers a second possible purpose, יום טוב, and the challenge to that idea comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason, finalizing the purchase, was just rejected. Now the גמרא suggests the banging was about the rules of יום טוב. Birds in a dovecote normally need to be set aside ahead of time before they may be used on יום טוב. The full argument about this option continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A festival day, with its own rules about what may be used
If (used to list possible explanations one by one)
Setting something aside ahead of time so it may be used on יום טוב

phrases.english: If it was for the Festival,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the 'acquisition' reason in step 36, the גמרא turns to a second possible reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the banging was meant to prepare the birds for יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The challenge to this option is only being set up here, and it continues past this point.
